summary: Keep a still fill that takes the container's shape separate from a continuity flow with a volume rate, and never let a scrolling texture stand in for either.
objective: Change retained volume and its corresponding level or footprint according to basin geometry without implying a current; conserve section flow rates only in the declared incompressible branch without accumulation or sources between sections.
applies_when: A liquid is used as a covering, flood, tank level or pond rather than as decoration only.
A channel, hose or nozzle is used to talk about how fast volume moves.
intent_signals: fill the pond without making a river
narrow the pipe and speed up the jet
example_prompts: Let me raise a cistern level so more of the courtyard is covered, with no current implied.
Show a hose and nozzle where the same volume flow gets faster in the narrower section.
negative_signals: UV-scrolling water that claims to be a current.
A fill slider that also moves boats as if there were a river.
not_for: Predicting turbulent mixing, viscous velocity profiles or pressure losses, or compressible gas dynamics; continuity bookkeeping alone does not provide those models.
Claims that a coverage texture conserves mass.

principles: Coverage is retained volume occupying a basin; flow is volume crossing a section per unit time. Neither is inferred from a scrolling texture.
In the still constant-density branch p=p0+rho g h, with h depth below the horizontal free surface.

Q=A v uses section-average normal velocity. Equality of station flow rates requires no accumulation or intervening sources; viscosity does not remove mass conservation, though this record predicts no detailed velocity profile.
implementation: Coverage owns retained volume V in a declared basin, with monotone capacity function V(h) from its interior geometry. Solve h for V, including dry/fully filled endpoints. Clamp retained volume at capacity and report excess as overflow; do not silently discard it.

For still fluid in uniform gravity use a horizontal free surface clipped to the basin. A deliberately tilted or decorative surface is display-only, excluded from hydrostatic volume and pressure claims.

Flow owns positive section areas and Q. At fixed sections with no accumulation, branches or sources between them, set section-average normal velocity v=Q/A. This specifies transport, not a viscous profile or pressure-loss prediction.

Pause freezes model time and tracer advancement while preserving Q and retained volume. Reset restores initial fill, Q, tracer state and time; switching models updates the readout and its stated assumptions.
observable_checks: Increasing retained volume within capacity increases level according to V(h); horizontal footprint may stay constant in a vertical-sided tank. Overflow is explicitly reported.
At fixed Q with no accumulation, halving a positive station area doubles the section-average speed.
Changing normal-map scrolling alone changes neither V nor Q. Pausing retains both values and resumes tracer advancement without resetting its state.

creative_affordances: Stylised ponds, ink fills or molten metal can still use a volume-owned free surface.
Optional streamlines belong to the flow model and should be hideable in coverage mode.
known_limits: Equal section volume rates assume constant density and no accumulation between stations; compressible flow requires mass-flux accounting.
Hydrostatic p = p0 + rho g h is for constant density; it is not a shallow-water wave solver.
Authored reusable guidance; no runtime artifact has been observed for this record.

claims.statement: Liquids have definite volumes but take the shape of their container; in a fluid of constant density the pressure at depth h is p = p0 + rho g h.
claims.scope: Still fluid of constant density as in OpenStax 14.1; not flowing or stratified fluid.

source_refs.locator: 14.1, liquids take container shape; pressure at a depth p=p0+rho g h

claims.statement: Volume flow rate is Q=A v where v is the section-average normal velocity. For incompressible flow with no sources, sinks or accumulation between sections, conservation gives A1 v1=A2 v2.
claims.scope: Constant-density flow through fixed sections; no velocity-profile or viscous pressure-loss prediction, and no compressible-gas approximation.

source_refs.locator: 14.5, Eq14.13 Q=Av with average speed; conservation of mass and continuity
